reason: E1 directly shows that high strength in NbTaTiV and CrMoNbV is attributable to edge dislocations, supporting the premise that edge dislocations are dominant. However, E1 does not address the effect of cold deformation (HPT) on dislocation populations, nor does it provide evidence that HPT specifically increases edge dislocation density or that lattice distortion pins them—these mechanistic steps are not supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Cold deformation (HPT) increases edge dislocation density in refractory HEAs
Edge dislocations are the dominant strength-limiting carriers in these alloys
Lattice distortion in refractory HEAs pins edge dislocations and elevates glide barriers
Increased edge dislocation density and pinning cause the observed high hardness/strength
